- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.2) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid underestimating rebound.
- After sharp price spikes (forecast > true by >5%), model often over-optimistically continues upward; cap next-period forecast at 1–2% below peak or align with recent 5-day moving average.
- If sentiment is positive (≥0.4) and price is trending up, model frequently overestimates momentum; reduce forecast slope by 10–15% in next 3–5 periods.
- When true price deviates from 30-day moving average by >3%, model often fails to mean-revert; apply a 2–3 period lag correction: if forecast is >MA+3%, reduce by 1–2% per period until convergence.
- If sentiment is negative and price is falling, model often underestimates depth; add 0.5–1.5% buffer to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.
- For 30-day forecasts, if last 3 true values show strong downward trend, model often fails to recognize it; apply a 1–2% downward bias to forecast if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- If sentiment is volatile (alternating 0.2–0.4), model tends to oscillate; smooth forecast by averaging last 3–5 values or apply exponential decay with α=0.3 to reduce noise.
